extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing manuscripts for the Journal of Fluid Mechanics (researchers in fluid mechanics preparing JFM submissions)
extracted.subtask_description: Journal of Fluid Mechanics house style and notation guidance for preparing manuscripts (layout, math notation, figures/tables, references, spelling, units, abbreviations). Targeted at authors submitting papers to JFM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: The title should be simple and concise. Only the first word is capitalized, apart from proper names. If the paper is part of a series then the title is styled ‘Annular flow. Part 3. Experiments’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use minimal capitalization; treat series with the ‘Part N’ format. Avoid long or overly detailed titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors and affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors’ names appear together on the same line, capitalized. Addresses are listed separately below, with a superscript numeral to link each author to the appropriate address if there are more than one. Postal addresses must be given in full, including zip codes or the equivalent, and the country. E-mail address(es) can follow on a separate line. A new address can be indicated in a footnote to the author’s name if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full postal addresses and country; use superscript numerals for multiple affiliations; include email on separate line; the Editorial Office inserts received/revised dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract content
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should be self-contained and self-explanatory and contain a summary of purpose, methodology, results and conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid references and displayed equations in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section heading style
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the first word of the heading is capitalized, apart from proper names. In the text use the symbol § instead of spelling out the word ‘section’, except at the start of a sentence. Section headings are bold, so any maths symbols not normally bold, i.e. not vectors, should be changed to italic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use § within sentences; ensure math in bold headings uses appropriate sloping/italic forms per Input Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any financial support should be mentioned here. Dedications are not normally permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep acknowledgements focused on funding and technical/administrative help; avoid personal dedications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices placement and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Any appendices appear between the acknowledgements and the references and are labelled A, B, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long detailed appendices of interest to a few readers only are not printed, but made available as a supplement to the online version of the paper or from the Editorial Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: References: ordering and content
rubrics_metrics.description: References are listed at the end of the paper in strict alphabetical order. If the same author(s) has more than one publication in the same year, then a, b, etc. should be added after the year. Private communications are not included in the References; when they are mentioned in the text, initials of first names must be given. Articles that are ‘submitted’ or ‘in press’ may be included provided that the full title and the name of the Journal are given. Non-published material not widely available should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles and last page numbers are preferred but may be omitted consistently; include thesis titles; do not add publisher addresses except where needed for University Presses; conference proceedings must include editor(s) and publisher; follow JFM style and short journal-title conventions (World List of Scientific Periodicals).

rubrics_metrics.name: References in text (citation style)
rubrics_metrics.description: References in the text should include the author(s) name, and the year in parentheses, unless the reference is already in parentheses, e.g. see Smith (1989) or (see Smith 1989). Strings of references in parentheses should be in date order and separated by semicolons, with no commas before the dates, e.g. (Jones 1967, 1978; Tam 1980; Dog 1991).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are three authors, all names are given on first mention, then first name and et al. subsequently. When there are four or more authors et al. is used from the start. Page/section numbers follow the date, after a comma (e.g. Smith (1987, p. 234)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure numbering and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures with captions may either be placed within the text with an eps file supplied or at the end with a separate list of captions. Figures must be numbered sequentially in the order in which they are mentioned in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide eps files or dummy space in text; avoid large white areas; choose aspect ratios that use space well (not too tall/thin).

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure content and captions
rubrics_metrics.description: Complicated information should appear in the caption rather than on the figure. Avoid duplicating information on the figure and in the caption. Groups of similar figures should be numbered as parts (a), (b), etc. of the same figure, with a single caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep figures visually clear; put explanatory details in captions; number groups as figure 1(a), 1(b) etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure references and labels
rubrics_metrics.description: In the text, the word ‘figure’ is never abbreviated, and only capitalized at the start of a sentence. Do not put parentheses around a, b etc. if the phrase is already in parentheses. Examples of forms: figure 1; figure 1(a, b); figure 1(a–e); figures 1(a) and 1(b); (figure 1a,b); (figures 1a and 1b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the un-abbreviated word figure and follow the example forms for referring to subparts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table numbering, captions, and numeric formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables must be numbered sequentially in the order in which they are mentioned in the text. The word ‘table’ is only capitalized at the start of a sentence. Each should have a caption. There should be zeros before decimal points for numbers less than one, and powers of 10 rather than ‘e-4’ etc. should be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive detailed tables of interest to a few readers only will not be printed but made available as a supplement to the online version or from the Editorial Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layout of displayed equations and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Long, complicated or important equations are displayed, and punctuated as part of the text. Numbered equations appear on separate lines, but related equations may be denoted (2a), (2b), etc. and if they are short, they should be on the same line, separated by a space, and then numbered in the style (2a, b), (2a–c) etc. Two or more equations on separate lines but with the same number should be braced together. Displayed equations are centred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break long equations before a + or − where possible; use a multiplication sign if the break must be at a product; punctuate displayed equations as part of sentences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fractions and in-text equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Small fractions should be used for numerals (but not symbols) in single-line displayed equations. To save space, short simple fractions should be typed with a slash rather than on two lines. Super- or subscript fractions are always one line, e.g. 1/2 not 1 over 2. Non-displayed equations within the text must be short and simple, and fractions must be on one line only, with a slash, i.e. gh/u not gh over u.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use slash style (a/b) for inline fractions; avoid multi-line stacked fractions in text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equation references in text
rubrics_metrics.description: When equations are referred to in the text, only the number in parentheses need be given, e.g. ‘substituting (3.12) into (3.20) we obtain...’ The word ‘Equation’ is only needed at the start of a sentence and should never be abbreviated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using numerals in parentheses for any other reason; use the parenthesized equation number alone for references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical fonts: roman vs italic vs bold
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical symbols are usually printed in the italic or sloping greek type normally produced by LaTeX. Non-italic fonts should be used as follows: Roman type should be used for mathematical operations (e.g. sin, log, d for differential), constants (e.g. i, e, exp), Ai, Bi (Airy functions), Re, Im (real, imaginary), physical units (cm, s, etc.), abbreviations such as c.c. and h.o.t. Greek letters are slanted for mathematical variables, but constants such as pi and mu (micro) and operators such as ∆ are upright. Bold italic or bold sloping greek for vectors; bold sloping sans serif for tensors and matrices; script as an alternative when same letter denotes different quantities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid multiletter symbols such as KE (use EK instead) except for dimensionless numbers like Re, Pr; when using two-letter symbols keep spacing smaller than normal LaTeX math mode. See Input Guide for LaTeX specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of product symbols and scalar product
rubrics_metrics.description: A symbol is not normally used to denote a product: use a multiplication symbol only when breaking a displayed equation, for vector products or between numbers. Use a centred point only for the scalar product of vectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer implicit juxtaposition for products except in the listed exceptions; use centered dot for scalar products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large-number formatting and order notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Large numbers that are not scientific powers should not include commas, but have the form 1600 or 16 000 or 160 000. Use O to denote ‘of the order of’, not the LaTeX \mathcal{O}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not write commas in large numbers; use spaces or no separator; use plain O for order notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units and unit formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: The International System of Units (SI) should normally be used, with an exponent not a solidus, e.g. cm s−1 not cm/s. There should be a space between a number and its units, and there is no need to repeat the units in a list, e.g. 5 and 6 cm. Use % instead of writing out ‘per cent’ and ◦ instead of ‘degrees’. On a figure the axis label should be (deg.) rather than using the symbol by each number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a low (not centered) decimal point; use exponents rather than slashes for unit combinations; include a space between numeral and unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations: definition and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Only commonly accepted abbreviations can be used, and they must be defined at first occurrence. There should be points between lower-case letters in an abbreviation, but not between capital letters, e.g. p.d.f., r.m.s. and LES. There is no point after a contraction, engng for example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the following abbreviations: 2-D, 3-D, l.h.s., r.h.s., fig., eq. Define any abbreviation at first use and then use consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling and capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Use British spelling conforming to the preferred spelling in the Shorter Oxford English Dictionary (e.g. behaviour, colour, centre, travelling, modelling, emphasize, zeroth, analyse). Use initial capital letters for proper names and their derivatives, e.g. Gaussian, Lagrangian, Cartesian, Pitot. Figure, table, section should not be capitalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Shorter OED preferred forms; capitalize proper names only; do not capitalize generic words like figure/table/section except at sentence start.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation and hyphenation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyphens should be used between compound adjectives when preceding a noun (e.g. high-frequency wave, solid-body rotation, first-order equation). Self-, cross- and half- are always followed by a hyphen, and a hyphen follows ‘non’, apart from nonlinear. Nouns with prefixes and compound nouns should normally be one word unless there is a repeated letter. En rules (keyed as a double hyphen) should be used when replacing ‘and’ or ‘to’, e.g. gravity–capillary, Navier–Stokes, 10–20 cm. A comma is not needed after an abbreviating point (e.g. e.g. or i.e.) nor between lists of adjectives. When a complete sentence is inside parentheses, then so is the final full stop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply hyphenation only where specified (compound adjectives before nouns); use double hyphen for en rule in plain text; follow examples for one-word vs two-word compounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid footnotes and separate nomenclature lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid footnotes since they interrupt the reading of the text. Separate lists of nomenclature are not normally permitted. Symbols should be defined and explained on first appearance in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If many symbols are needed, consider online supplement for extended nomenclature; always define symbols at first use in the main text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Italics usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Italics should seldom be used for emphasis, but may be needed in definitions and for foreign words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve italics for technical/definitional purposes and foreign terms; avoid using italics as casual emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: General quick-reference math/font rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a roman typeface in maths for: the d (or D) operator in differentials and integrals; i (square root of −1); e (exponential); units and abbreviations. Use appropriate typeface for vectors, matrices and tensors. Put punctuation after equations where appropriate. For fractions within the text use e.g. gh/u not gh over u, and similarly 1/2 not a stacked fraction for superscripts and subscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these common quick rules consistently; consult the Input Guide for precise LaTeX commands.
